skim: President Trump declared a Russia–Ukraine “energy ceasefire” on Truth Social, but Volodymyr Zelensky told Axios the announcement was “news for me” and asked Trump to say when it would actually begin, as Moscow left the claim unconfirmed.

A second Houthi strike hit Riyadh airport’s domestic terminals a day after an attack that killed 12, as Trump weighed joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis and Lufthansa extended its flight suspension through Oct 16.

A landslide dammed Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki river and the resulting flood swept away a dozen houses and three bridges in Gorkha district, leaving five missing — two months after a glacier-collapse flood killed 1,457 people in the same river basin.

Manchester City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield, sending Ryan Gravenberch off, to lead the Premier League alone with six wins from six — while Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix from pole for his 73rd career victory.

UK Chancellor John Healey is weighing a windfall levy and a temporary petrol VAT cut to close a £35 billion Budget gap, as Delhi police held nearly 3,000 “Cockroach Party” protesters and India rejected the UN’s criticism of the crackdown as “unwarranted interference.”

stories.headline: Landslide-Dammed River Floods Nepal Village, Leaving Five Missing
stories.body: A dry landslide blocked the Budhi Gandaki river on Saturday above Chumnubri village in Nepal’s Gorkha district, and the resulting flood swept away about a dozen houses, two suspension bridges and a highway bridge linking Gorkha with Dhading district, per Al Jazeera (Oct 11). Nepal’s disaster authority said two women and three men remain missing despite rescuing at least 82 people, including nine foreigners, while local official Laxmi Gurung called the flood “very scary” and said “it still feels like a nightmare for us.” The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, where a glacier collapse in August triggered a catastrophic flood that killed 1,457 people with thousands still missing, and authorities have now warned residents downstream in Tanahun, Chitwan and the Nawalparasi districts.

stories.headline: Panama Hit by Twin Earthquakes and 45 Aftershocks, Tsunami Warnings Issued
stories.body: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake struck Panama’s Pacific coast on Friday, followed by a second magnitude-6.6 quake and more than 45 aftershocks recorded by the University of Panama, per Fox Carolina/AP (Oct 9). The US Geological Survey put the epicenter near Pitaloza Arriba in Herrera province; a historic building’s tower and several balconies collapsed in Penonomé, one person was hit by falling debris, cracks appeared in the Penonomé cathedral, and Tocumen International Airport briefly suspended operations. The US National Weather Service issued tsunami warnings for Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala, while President José Raúl Mulino urged calm, writing on X that “what happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder.”

stories.headline: Manchester City Go Top Alone, Beating 10-Man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield
stories.body: Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored in a 16-minute second-half spell as Manchester City beat Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday, per NBC Sports (Oct 11). Liverpool played the last half-hour with 10 men after Ryan Gravenberch was shown a second yellow card for clipping Doku, and the defeat was new manager Andoni Iraola’s first since taking charge. City moved to 18 points from six straight wins to lead the Premier League alone, with Liverpool on nine points from six games.

stories.headline: Verstappen Wins Singapore Grand Prix From Pole, His 73rd Career Victory
stories.body: Max Verstappen led every lap of the Singapore Grand Prix to beat Charles Leclerc by 7.335 seconds, winning on his 250th Grand Prix start for his first Singapore victory and 73rd career win, per Formula1.com (Oct 11). Kimi Antonelli finished third to extend his championship lead, while Gabriel Bortoleto, Lance Stroll and Franco Colapinto all retired with mechanical problems that triggered two Virtual Safety Car periods. “It’s taken a while, but I think this race was very good,” Verstappen said. The win follows his victory in Saturday’s rain-hit Sprint, and the season resumes at the United States Grand Prix on Oct 23-25.

stories.headline: Australia Lead South Africa by 139 With All 10 Second-Innings Wickets in Hand
stories.body: Australia closed day three of the Durban Test at 33 without loss in their second innings, leading South Africa by 139 runs after bowling the hosts out for 284 in reply to Australia’s first-innings 390, per Cricket.com.au (Oct 11). With all 10 second-innings wickets intact, Australia are strongly placed to set South Africa a difficult target heading into the final two days of the series opener at Kingsmead.

stories.headline: Riyadh Airport Disruption Returns as Second Houthi Strike Hits Domestic Terminals
stories.body: Operations at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport were only “gradually returning to normal” after Thursday’s deadly strike when a second attack hit terminals 3 and 4 on Sunday, per CBS News and The National (Oct 9-11). Flightradar24 data showed cancellations easing from 43% on Thursday to 13% by Friday before the new strike reimposed disruption; Lufthansa has now suspended Riyadh flights through Oct 16, while Etihad, flydubai and several Indian and Saudi domestic carriers cancelled or rescheduled services around both attacks. Saudi authorities put the Saturday toll at 12 dead and 309 injured, including a US citizen.

stories.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google Refuse to Guarantee AI Safety Under Oath
stories.body: At a New York City Council hearing, representatives of OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google all declined to guarantee under oath that their AI agents would never cause catastrophic harm, per Fox News (Oct 5-6). OpenAI’s Morgan Dwyer said “it is not possible for me to commit or guarantee that any technology is without risk,” while Anthropic’s Logan Graham said “the science of doing this is fundamentally hard and unsettled.” Council Speaker Julie Menin said lawmakers were not asking for perfection but “accountability, transparency and safety overall,” as the council considers AI legislation; the same day, UN human rights chief Volker Türk called for mandatory AI safeguards.

stories.headline: SoftBank Completes $64.6bn Total Stake in OpenAI With Final $10bn Payment
stories.body: SoftBank closed the final tranche of its $30 billion commitment to OpenAI, bringing its cumulative investment to $64.6 billion for roughly a 13% stake, per The Star/Bloomberg (Oct 1-2). The completed round follows SoftBank chief Masayoshi Son’s aggressive push into AI infrastructure and comes as OpenAI and Anthropic both pursue mega-valuations — OpenAI reportedly seeking fresh funding near a $1.4 trillion valuation and Anthropic eyeing a $2 trillion IPO — that analysts have increasingly questioned on financial grounds.

stories.headline: Trump Claims Russia-Ukraine “Energy Ceasefire,” Zelensky Says It’s “News for Me”
stories.body: Trump posted on Truth Social that “effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine,” claiming both sides had agreed, per Axios (Oct 11). Volodymyr Zelensky told Axios the announcement “was news for me,” adding, “if President Trump negotiated it with Putin, please tell us when the ceasefire begins” — Russia has not confirmed any deal, and Trump made a similar unconfirmed claim last month. The announcement follows days of friction after Trump eased sanctions on Russian diesel exports on Oct 9 and called for Ukraine to replace Zelensky on Oct 10; separately on ABC, Zelensky said Ukraine would hold elections if Russia agreed to a 60-day ceasefire.

stories.headline: Second Houthi Strike Hits Riyadh Airport as Trump Weighs Joining Saudi Campaign
stories.body: A day after a Houthi missile killed 12 people and wounded over 300 at Riyadh’s airport, a second strike hit domestic terminals 3 and 4 on Sunday, per CBS News (Oct 11). Trump is considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US “strongly condemns the recent attacks on the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by the terrorist Houthis,” and Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that “the airports and airspace are exposed to targeting and constitute a theatre of operations for our forces.” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Iran’s proxies are “pushing the region into a spiral of violence.”

fixtures.headline: Second Test Moves to Gqeberha
fixtures.body: Australia and South Africa meet again at St George’s Park for the second of three Tests, immediately after the Durban opener concludes.

fixtures.body: Arsenal visit the City Ground and Chelsea play at Goodison Park's successor Hill Dickinson Stadium, while Manchester City host Ipswich at the Etihad in the Premier League's seventh round.

fixtures.headline: Season Resumes at the United States Grand Prix
fixtures.body: The paddock heads to the Circuit of the Americas in Austin for practice, qualifying and the race, as Antonelli looks to defend the championship lead he extended in Singapore.

portfolio.headline: Cloudflare Extends Rally Alongside Cloud-Infrastructure Peers, No Single Catalyst Found
portfolio.body: Cloudflare rose alongside Oracle, CrowdStrike and Twilio this week as the cloud and dev-infrastructure basket extended a rally tied to continued enthusiasm for agentic-AI infrastructure spending; no single company-specific announcement was found for the move, and it reads as a sector-wide rotation rather than individual news.

portfolio.headline: Oracle Rises With the Same Cloud-Infrastructure Basket
portfolio.body: Oracle moved with Cloudflare, CrowdStrike and Twilio this week; see the Cloudflare entry above for the connected read — no distinct, dated announcement specific to Oracle was found for the session.

portfolio.headline: Arm Holdings Gives Back Ground as Chip Names Pull Back
portfolio.body: Arm Holdings slipped this week against a broader pullback in chip names; no fresh company-specific announcement was found for the session, and the move reads as giveback after the stock's strong 2026 run rather than a reaction to new news.

stories.headline: Modi Opens First Stretch of Chennai Metro Phase 2, Riding It With TN CM Vijay
stories.body: PM Modi inaugurated the first 14.6km stretch of Chennai Metro Phase 2 between Poonamallee Bypass and Vadapalani, riding the new Yellow Line with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay, per WION and ConstructionWorld (Oct 11). The stretch connects to the existing network via a skywalk at the Vadapalani interchange and is the first section of the city's planned east-west metro link through its western suburbs to open to passengers.

stories.headline: India Rejects UN Criticism of Nearly 3,000 Detentions at “Cockroach Party” Protest
stories.body: India's mission to the UN rejected the OHCHR's criticism of Delhi's crackdown on Cockroach Janata Party protesters as “unwarranted interference in the country's internal affairs,” per Indian Defence News (Oct 11). The UN body, through spokesman Thameen Al-Kheetan, had said it was “concerned by reports of mass detentions” of demonstrators, lawyers and journalists and urged “utmost restraint” by police; India countered that it is “the world's largest democracy” with courts available for legal remedies and said the UN should apply the same scrutiny to large protests elsewhere. Delhi Police had detained nearly 3,000 people, including CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, as they tried to reach Jantar Mantar for a sit-in demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation; most were later released.

stories.headline: Chancellor Healey Weighs Windfall Levy and Petrol VAT Cut to Close £35bn Budget Gap
stories.body: Chancellor John Healey faces a roughly £35 billion funding gap ahead of his first Budget on Oct 28, driven by rising health spending, a planned increase in defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030, and higher borrowing costs that have roughly halved the government's fiscal headroom, per Time News/Bloomberg (Oct 12). Healey is reportedly weighing an oil and gas windfall levy, a tax on excess bank profits and a temporary petrol VAT cut, while keeping Labour's pledge not to raise VAT, National Insurance or income tax; PM Andy Burnham has rejected funding defence shortfalls by cutting welfare. The IFS warned the Treasury against relying on unrealistic spending cuts, saying that would make the Budget “a work of fiction,” while Healey has said his aim is to give households economic “breathing space.”

stories.headline: Qatar's Al-Kaabi Calls for Keeping Energy “Above Politics” at Riyadh Forum
stories.body: Qatar's Minister of State for Energy Affairs Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi called for a new world energy order in which energy is “kept above politics and is never made a victim or target of conflict,” speaking at the 17th International Energy Forum Ministerial Meeting in Riyadh, per The Peninsula (Oct 11). Al-Kaabi said the regional conflict has caused “by far, the world's worst energy crisis,” affecting roughly 20% of global hydrocarbon supplies and causing tens of billions of dollars in damage to energy infrastructure, and offered Qatar's “unwavering solidarity” with Saudi Arabia over the Riyadh airport attacks. “Energy security must unite us, not divide us,” he said. “It must be protected, not weaponized.”
